title: Περὶ κοσμοποιίας / De opificio mundi — John Philoponus, On the Creation of the World (RU «О сотворении мира»); pilot Book III
author: John Philoponus (Ioannes Grammaticus)
date: c. 546–560 CE (dedicated to Sergius of Antioch)
size: 7 books; Reichardt Teubner c. 300 pp.; est. 85–95k words (estimate)
edition: Reichardt, Teubner 1897, public domain: https://archive.org/details/joannisphiliponi00philuoft. Scholten, Fontes Christiani 23 (1997), Greek–German, copyrighted.
ru_evidence: Excerpts only: Benevich, Антология восточно-христианской богословской мысли II (2009), pp. 55–62 (ruwiki Иоанн Филопон). Ogovitsin, commentary on IV.4, ΣΧΟΛΗ 20.2 (2026). No full translation found.
en_evidence: The enwiki article on Philoponus' De opificio lists only Reichardt and Scholten's German. An Open Library search returns only Teubner and Herder editions. No English translation found.
other_translations: German: C. Scholten, Über die Erschaffung der Welt (Herder 1997, 3 vols). Other languages: none found.
value: Philoponus' late Christian synthesis of Alexandrian science. It applies impetus dynamics to the heavens and to light and cosmography, and attacks Theodore of Mopsuestia's (and Cosmas') cosmos. A key text for history of science and theology, Byzantine exegesis and the reception of Basil's Hexaemeron.
ai_feasibility: High. Clear technical prose, a public-domain Greek text, and abundant parallels (CAG, Basil). Risks: dense scientific terminology and the Antiochene polemical context. The German version can serve for cross-checking.
pilot_unit: Book III (firmament, Gen 1:6–8; critique of the tabernacle-shaped cosmos), about 12–15k words (estimate). Alternative: prooemium plus Book I.
